metadata.title: A social network analysis of student-perceived teaching practices in top-performing countries and regions in reading literacy: Insights from PISA 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 Student Survey data for 16 top-performing countries and regions in reading literacy, but the methodology does not report the use of PISA sampling weights or any specific weight variable (e.g., student design weights) in the descriptive, clustering, or network estimation steps. Instead, the authors explicitly draw a stratified simple random sample without replacement of 1,000 students per country/region for the social network analysis, yielding 16,000 students total, which suggests a design-based representativeness is not fully preserved in the network stage. Because the paper does not discuss complex survey design adjustments (stratification/clustering) or replicate-weight procedures, the results should be interpreted as descriptive/structural comparisons of teaching-practice networks rather than population-representative estimates. No PV-based achievement scaling is modeled as an outcome; the dependent constructs are IRT-derived latent variables for perceived teaching practices.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not model cognitive achievement plausible values (PISA PVs) as an outcome; instead, it analyzes IRT-synthesized latent variables representing students’ perceived teaching practices (e.g., disciplinary climate, teacher support) and then applies clustering and social network analysis. Because the dependent variables are not PV-based achievement scores, PV handling is not applicable. The manuscript also does not report a specific missing-data strategy for the teaching-practice items/IRT estimation, so missing-data handling is treated as not reported rather than inferred.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analysis uses PISA 2018 Student Survey Database and focuses on 16 countries/regions identified as top-performing in reading literacy. Canada is excluded because of missing components in the student questionnaire regarding language teachers, leaving 16 countries/regions. For the social network analysis, the authors apply a stratified simple random sampling without replacement to select exactly 1,000 students per country/region, producing an analytic network sample of 16,000 students. Teaching-practice items are recoded so that reverse-worded items in disciplinary climate, teacher support, and teacher-directed instruction reflect more favorable perceptions, and then analyzed with IRT to synthesize latent variables (theta-values) for each teaching-practice construct.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (Student Survey) — perceived teaching practices (IRT latent variables)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Strength centrality across countries/regions: teacher support mean strength=0.90; teacher enthusiasm=0.83; cognitive stimulation=0.80; adaptive instruction=0.74; teacher-directed instruction=0.73; disciplinary climate=0.32. Additional analysis (Teaching-practice network structure (partial correlations)): Partial correlation networks estimated per country/region; network stability assessed via nonparametric bootstrap (1000 resamples) with strength centrality stability CS cor = 0.70 (all coefficients > 0.5). Additional analysis (Teaching-practice cluster membership (4-cluster typology)): Hierarchical clustering on country/region average teaching-practice scores produced 4 clusters; variance analysis showed significant inter-cluster differences for all six practices (e.g., disciplinary climate F=332317.03***; teacher support F=99230.10***; teacher-directed instruction F=99668.59***; adaptive instruction F=78231.26***; cognitive stimulation F=101427.46***; teacher enthusiasm F=85513.49***).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading (Student Survey) the study leveraged teacher support, teacher enthusiasm, cognitive stimulation, adaptive instruction, and disciplinary climate to estimate strength centrality in teaching-practice networks, finding that teacher support was the most central practice on average (mean strength=0.90), followed by teacher enthusiasm (0.83) and cognitive stimulation (0.80), while disciplinary climate was comparatively less central (0.32). This indicates that prioritizing timely, individualized teacher support may be the most actionable starting point for designing instructional improvement strategies, while recognizing that network roles can vary by country/region.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2018 Reading (Student Survey) data for 16 top-performing countries/regions in reading literacy, using IRT to synthesize students’ perceived teaching-practice items into latent variables (theta-values) for six constructs: disciplinary climate, teacher support, teacher-directed instruction, cognitive stimulation, adaptive instruction, and teacher enthusiasm. For the social network analysis, the authors draw a stratified simple random sample of 1,000 students per country/region (16,000 total) and estimate partial-correlation networks, applying LASSO regularization (gamma=0.5) to obtain sparser networks. Network stability is evaluated via nonparametric bootstrap (1000 resamples), reporting strength centrality stability (CS cor=0.70). Across countries/regions, teacher support is the most central practice (mean strength=0.90), and clustering yields four typologies with significant inter-cluster differences for all six practices. Limitations include the descriptive nature of network/clustering results (no PV-based achievement outcome modeling) and missing-data handling not being reported.
